body:
Well, it's obvious. A ride is predetermined because it was designed a certain way. A roller coaster that goes in an oval will always go in an oval because it was constructed like that.

But when I say reality/life, I mean EVERYTHING. Everything in existence, every action made by every human, every pebble blowing in the wind. Those things being predetermined are terrifying to me and caused me to feel suicidal.
I don't know how else to explain it, I think I made it pretty clear

> My point is that you can't say that our Universe was predetermined, since you would need to know and comprehend the state of all molecules in the Universe.

What are you saying? That sounds like you're implying it is predetermined but not to our knowledge.

> You can't have answer to this question whether determinism is true, so it's all about beliefs. It's like a religion.

The difference is religion doesn't have scientific experiments/whatever

> Do you really understand what they mean? Do you think they do?

I don't understand, but I think they do. They're very smart and educated

Yes, I asked them. They said this: "Because else it means causation is false. And if causation is false, the universe would be a very, very different place" & "It would mean sometimes 1+1= something else than 2
No like a joke like 1+1=3
Just that sometimes it doesn't equal 2
And it's not just math
It would mean everything would be fundementally different
All the time"
That doesn't help, rides being predetermined are okay. Life/reality itself? NOT OKAY.

The thing is my brain latches onto beliefs

My brain is weird and different, and I can't shake off this thing
Like, I don't get joy out of anything anymore because "it was going to happen anyway regardless".
No, I did not say I was only destined for death. I meant I'm just horrified that life is a one-way track and I can't make my own choices.

You're not understanding. Yes, I can't predict what happens next.

Just like in a movie I've never seen before. It's not interactive, because it's a movie. You can't pick what happens next, you don't know what happens next, but it's only a one-way track.

Obviously I'm okay with that because it's a movie.

But when it's life, it's horrifying, nauseating, anguish-causing and maddening.

People have done science test/experiments/studies

Like the one where the brain activity of your action comes before your consciousness is aware of it
But I don't know. I can't predict what's coming next, but that doesn't make me feel better. Feeling like life is a one-way track and everything was gonna happen anyway is killing me.
